method: Single OpenStreetMap node (place=village, name='Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station'), Overpass extract with out geom; using the near-pole bbox form (-90,-180,-89.98,180) as instructed, mirrors overpass-api.de then lz4.overpass-api.de. No OSM building footprint for the station or a separate IceCube Laboratory (ICL) feature was found in this query (a name-pattern search for 'Amundsen|South Pole Station' on building ways, and for 'IceCube Laboratory|ICL' on any way, returned zero elements; only this one place node matched). Used as a visible reference marker for site:south-pole-icecube's approximate location, not a claim about the true surveyed position of the array, the ICL building, or any structure; accuracy_m is set generously (300 m) because a single untagged-building 'place' node is not a survey. The node sits about 223 m from the geometric South Pole (90 - 89.998 degrees of latitude), plausible for the station's real offset from the pole marker.
name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station (reference marker)
notes: This marker stands in for site:south-pole-icecube on the map, the same way geometry:meyrin-site-marker stands in for site:cern-meyrin on map:cern. site:south-pole-ara is NOT covered by this marker (it is a physically distinct site ~2 km away with no sourced position of its own this session) and is listed in map.unlocated[] instead.

summary.plain: An approximate marker for the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station and the IceCube array beside it; not a survey of any building or the detector itself.
